title: Witness LIM a for the least upper bound of a nonempty bounded set of reals (Theorem 5.5.9)
intent: Prove Theorem 5.5.9, that every nonempty set of reals bounded above has a least upper bound, by building a rational approximation a from the rounding lemma LUB_claim1, turning the adjacent-term bound LUB_claim2 into Cauchyness via LIM_of_Cauchy, and exhibiting S := LIM a as the witness, with LIM_of_ge and LIM_of_le discharging the upper-bound and minimality halves of IsLUB.

parent.name: Real.LUB_exist
parent.statement: theorem Real.LUB_exist {E: Set Real} (hE: Set.Nonempty E) (hbound: BddAbove E): ∃ S, IsLUB E S

children.name: Real.LUB_claim1
children.statement:
lemma Real.LUB_claim1 (n : ℕ) {E: Set Real} (hE: Set.Nonempty E) (hbound: BddAbove E)
:  ∃! m:ℤ,
      (((m:ℚ) / (n+1):ℚ):Real) ∈ upperBounds E
      ∧ ¬ (((m:ℚ) / (n+1) - 1 / (n+1):ℚ):Real) ∈ upperBounds E
children.closed_by: its own proof (lines 121-145): `existsUnique_of_exists_of_unique`, existence by `upperBound_between`/`upperBound_upper`, uniqueness by `grind [upperBound_discrete_unique]`
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: For each n there is a unique integer m such that m/(n+1) is an upper bound of E but (m/(n+1) − 1/(n+1)) is not.

children.name: Real.LUB_claim2
children.statement:
lemma Real.LUB_claim2 {E : Set Real} (N:ℕ) {a b: ℕ → ℚ}
  (hb : ∀ n, b n = 1 / (↑n + 1))
  (hm1 : ∀ (n : ℕ), ↑(a n) ∈ upperBounds E)
  (hm2 : ∀ (n : ℕ), ↑((a - b) n) ∉ upperBounds E)
: ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ n' ≥ N, |a n - a n'| ≤ 1 / (N+1)
children.closed_by: its own proof (lines 152-163): `abs_le`, each half by `upperBound_upper` then `gcongr`/`linarith`
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: If a n is always an upper bound of E and (a−b) n never is (b n = 1/(n+1)), then |a n − a n'| ≤ 1/(N+1) for all n, n' ≥ N.

children.name: Real.LIM_of_Cauchy
children.statement:
theorem Real.LIM_of_Cauchy {q:ℕ → ℚ} (hq: ∀ M, ∀ n ≥ M, ∀ n' ≥ M, |q n - q n'| ≤ 1 / (M+1)) :
    (q:Sequence).IsCauchy ∧ ∀ M, |q M - LIM q| ≤ 1 / (M+1)
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: A sequence with the adjacent-term bound 1/(M+1) is Cauchy, and its limit is within 1/(M+1) of each term.

children.name: Real.LIM.harmonic
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: The limit of 1/(n+1) is 0.

children.name: Real.LIM_of_ge
children.statement:
theorem Real.LIM_of_ge {x:Real} {a:ℕ → ℚ} (hcauchy: (a:Sequence).IsCauchy) (h: ∀ n, a n ≥ x) :
    LIM a ≥ x
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: If a Cauchy sequence of rationals is pointwise ≥ x, then its limit is ≥ x.

children.name: Real.LIM_of_le
children.statement:
theorem Real.LIM_of_le {x:Real} {a:ℕ → ℚ} (hcauchy: (a:Sequence).IsCauchy) (h: ∀ n, a n ≤ x) :
    LIM a ≤ x
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: If a Cauchy sequence of rationals is pointwise ≤ x, then its limit is ≤ x.

applicability.goal_shape: ∃ S, IsLUB E S — an existence goal whose witness is a limit (or supremum) built from a sequence of rational approximations; here the head symbol is the existential over the least-upper-bound predicate.
applicability.use_when: a concrete witness term is available (LIM a) and its two defining properties are already stated as named lemmas; the construction is a sequence whose Cauchyness and whose limiting upper-bound/minimality are separate, independently provable facts.
applicability.avoid_when: the witness cannot be named without first proving Cauchyness (here claim3 must come before `set S := LIM a`); when the approximating sequence is not Cauchy; when the two halves of the property (upper bound, minimality) are not both expressible as a pointwise-inequality limit lemma.

consequences: The witness move commits to one witness S := LIM a and then creates the two conjuncts of IsLUB as obligations: S an upper bound (discharged by LIM_of_ge) and S minimal (discharged by LIM_of_le). Before the witness can even be named, the approximating sequence a must be shown Cauchy (claim3 via LIM_of_Cauchy), and b must be Cauchy and tend to 0 (harmonic' and LIM.harmonic) so that S = LIM (a − b) holds. Four of the six leaves are stubbed with sorry in this source, so the glue compiles but the theorem is only as strong as those exercise holes. Failure modes: if a were not Cauchy the term LIM a would not be available to `use`; if the two halves needed a different limit lemma than LIM_of_ge/LIM_of_le, the pointwise-inequality transfer would not fit.
